:::{#def-prediction-bias}
#### Bias of a prediction

Let $\targetfn$ be a fixed function, and let $x_0$ be a point.
Let $\etargetfnf{x_0}$ be a [prediction](expectation.qmd#def-prediction) of the value $\targetfnf{x_0}$.
The prediction $\etargetfnf{x_0}$ is a random variable,
because it depends on the random training data.
The **bias** of $\etargetfnf{x_0}$ is

$$\bias{\etargetfnf{x_0}} \eqdef \E{\etargetfnf{x_0}} - \targetfnf{x_0}$$

:::

::: {.remark .notes}

In expected prediction error decompositions [@james2021islr2e, Section 2.2.2],
the bias reflects the error introduced by approximating a real-world relationship by a model.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-prediction-bias}
#### Computing the bias of a prediction

Suppose $\targetfnf{x_0} = 10$,
and the predictions $\etargetfnf{x_0}$,
over repeated training sets,
average $11$.
Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\bias{\etargetfnf{x_0}} &= 11 - 10 \\
&= 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

The squared bias is $1^2 = 1$,
the value in @exr-prediction-error.

:::
